_note: UI Next results lane fixture (provisional): anonymous answer rows per perspective (no name, no id, no free text but the board's quotes) for the ResultsAnswers and ResultsAnswersPhone boards. Questions and options are the pinned instrument's (seed/source/rubric_csv Items.csv + Options.csv, item ids below; the community options keep the board's added "I don't know"). Counts are aggregated from these rows by screens/results/data.js answerView(); the community rows reproduce the board's counts exactly. Split attributes (age, gender, met) are fixture values; a group under the minimum responses is hidden, as the board's footer says.

questions.q: Does your team have a translation brief or plan that defines what kind of translation you are aiming for?
options: Yes, we have a documented brief that defines our translation type and goals
Yes, we have a shared understanding as a team of what we are aiming for, but it is not documented
We are still working on defining our translation type and goals

questions.q: Before drafting, what does your team do to understand the meaning of the passage?
options: We study the passage using multiple resources (commentaries, original languages, etc.) and discuss as a team
We study the passage using at least one reference resource
We read the passage in a language we understand well and discuss it
We begin drafting based on our existing understanding

questions.q: How does your team check draft work internally before moving to external review?
options: The full team reviews every draft together
Every draft is checked by at least one other team member before moving forward
The lead translator or translation supervisor reviews drafts
Drafts are checked by another team member when there are questions or concerns
We move directly to external review without internal cross-checking

questions.q: As a group, how would we describe how easy or difficult this translation is to understand?
options: Most of it is easy, but some parts are hard
Much of it is difficult to understand

questions.q: Where we find it difficult, what makes it hard? (choose all that apply)
options: Some words are unfamiliar or strange
Some sentences are too long or complicated
It doesn't sound like the way we normally speak
others: "Some words sound like the neighbouring dialect, not ours."
"The chapter headings are fine but the verses run together."

questions.q: As a group, how often do we use this translation?
options: We use it about 3 times per week

questions.q: How confident are you that the translation team followed a sound and robust translation process?
options: I don't have enough information to say

questions.q: How confident are you in the translation team's understanding of the meaning of the original text?
options: I don't have enough information to say
